name: Average rule (sum form)
summary: Two H-boxes with labels a and b, connected through a NOT, give an H-box labelled a+b combined with a NOT-ed H-box labelled 2.
description:
A form of the [average rule](../zh-average/) that avoids dividing by 2. The left-hand side is the same, but the right-hand side combines an H-box with label $a+b$ and an H-box with label $2$ followed by a NOT (which is the state $2|0\rangle + |1\rangle$) in a Z-spider, giving $2|0\rangle + (a+b)|1\rangle$.

This version is used in the axiomatisation of the ZH-calculus over an arbitrary commutative ring $R$ in the 2021 completeness paper.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
